title: Difference between SIP and VoIP - GeeksforGeeks
content:
When it comes to communication over the Internet, two terms, SIP and VoIP are used often making many people confused. But one must stress that they are not the same while indicating their connection with the matter at hand. The confusion between SIP and VoIP needs to be clearly distinguished especially for those who are planning to use this type of communication system in their businesses or even themselves. This article gives one clarification to help distinguish one from the other to enable one to get exactly the technology that he/she requires.

What is SIP?

SIP or session initiation protocol is a protocol used to organize, control, and tear down real-time sessions between two or more parties via the Internet. Any form of communication such as voice, video, massaging, and other forms of media can happen in these sessions.

Advantages of SIP

  • Versatility: concerning this, it is important to note that SIP is not only designed to deliver voice calls, but can also serve as the platform for video and instant messaging as well as other forms of multimedia messages, which make SIP a suitable tool for implementing the concept of unified communications.
  • Scalability: SIP can also be implemented to incorporate more and more users and devices and this is advantageous especially when dealing with new establishments.
  • Interoperability: SIP is implemented and adopted more widely than other protocols and other platforms and gadgets are compatible with SIP system.

Disadvantages of SIP

  • Complexity: The application and management of SIP based systems are also other more complicated than the straightforward VoIP cases they are at times considered, this usually demands proper IT expertise.
  • Security Concerns: SIP like other Internet based protocols is open to security threats such as interception and denial of service (DoS) attacks in case certain security measures are not put in place.

What is VoIP?

VoIP is basically the transmission of voice, that is, communication that takes place over the internet, which is an abbreviation of Voice over Internet Protocol. It transcribes the human voice converting what is being said into digital packets suitable for transmission over the internet.

Advantages of VoIP

  • Cost-Effective: This is evident in that VoIP eliminates the use of the traditional phone lines opting instead to make use of the internet connection.
  • Flexibility: VoIP can be used on different platforms ranging from computers, smartphones and dedicated voice over IP phones meaning that flexibility of communication is present.
  • Advanced Features: In addition, VoIP is equipped with features such as call forwarding, voice mail, video call among others boosting the call experience.

Disadvantages of VoIP

  • Reliance on Internet Connection: The quality of VoIP depends a lot on the internet connection and it speed. Lack of adequate connectivity may cause one to drop a call or have a call with low quality audio.
  • Emergency Services Limitation: There are situations that the use of VoIP for making calls could result to inconsistent connectivity to emergency lines since VoIP could have difficulties in identifying caller’s location unlike the usual telephone systems.

Difference Between SIP and VoIP protocol

SIPVOIP
SIP stands for Session Initiation Protocol.Whereas VoIP stands for Voice over IP.
SIP can handle all types of media.While it can handles voice calls as well as messages.
SIP is more flexible.While it is a little bit flexible.
SIP is not depend any other device.But it depend on that devices which provide internet.
It is protocol of application layer.While it is Layer 3 network protocol.
It is related with signalling protocol to manipulate the technologies.Whereas it is related with Separate and severally noticeable technology.
It is compatible with internet.While it is also compatible with internet.
SIP uses severally systems for handling completely different operations.While it uses only particular system for handling entire operations.

Conclusion

SIP and VoIP are both popular integral technologies in the present day communication platforms, but different in functionality. VoIP is the technology for making voice calls that use the internet while SIP is one such protocol that can be used to handle calls as well as other media sessions. If a company needs a complete solution for its telecommunication needs then SIP is more advantageous than VoIP but if you want flexible and inexpensive solution for voice communication then VoIP can be a good choice for you. Knowledge of these distinctions will enable you to make proper decisions when either implementing a new communications system or when upgrading to a better one.
